original_question: Which subunit of ATP synthase is encoded by the gene associated with NARP syndrome?

final_qi.question: Which subunit of ATP synthase is encoded by the gene associated with NARP syndrome?
final_qi.long_answer: NARP (Neuropathy, Ataxia, and Retinitis Pigmentosa) syndrome is caused by pathogenic variants in the mitochondrial gene MT-ATP6. MT-ATP6 encodes the a-subunit (also called subunit 6) of the Fo sector of mitochondrial ATP synthase (complex V), which is essential for proton translocation and ATP production.

0.question: Which gene is associated with NARP syndrome?

final_answer.long_answer: NARP (neuropathy, ataxia and retinitis pigmentosa) results from pathogenic variants in the mitochondrial gene MT-ATP6 (also called ATP6). This gene encodes ATP synthase subunit a, the proton-conducting component of the Fo sector of mitochondrial ATP synthase (complex V). Mutations in MT-ATP6 impair proton translocation through subunit a, compromising ATP production and leading to the clinical features of NARP.
